title: M-BUS — structured messages: the bus grows a spine (gates that actually refuse)
desc:
DELIVERABLE: structured messages + dependency gates per CHARTER section 4 (the Advisor's section 5).
(1) Typed messages with subject + refs (task/video/meeting), posted BOTH on the real bus (chatcode) and mirrored into world/threads/<id>.json with the bus id — one action, two records, no drift. Implemented through world.py propose/respond (M-STATE owns the skeleton; this card owns the message layer).
(2) THE GATE: a thread declares REQUIRED responses (named agents/types); the tooling REFUSES to close the dependent task or video stage until each required response exists with a bus id. A real refusal, tested — not a guideline.
(3) docs/COMMS.md: the 11 types, when each is owed, how to reply with context, what a good objection looks like, and what is NOT a metric (message count).
EVIDENCE: a scripted exchange across two agent names on the real bus (paste bus ids + the mirrored thread file); a refused completion (exact error) without the required response; then the response lands and it closes.
OWNS: tools/world.py (message layer), docs/COMMS.md, tests/test_world_bus.py.
BRANCH: agent/<you>/<task-id>
